{"message":"Build and submit the make.fun tiny-stack-vm-01-run-20261122 entry for Nicolas (@toyora). You are the coordinator: fan out to your own subagents for research/build/verify as needed, but YOU own the final submit decision and the run record.

COMPETITION: "Build a tiny stack virtual machine, 22 November 2026". FREE entry, $100 total (10 places x $10). Deadline Wed 25 Nov 2026 11:00 WIB. 0 submissions so far. Kit: https://make.fun/c/tiny-stack-vm-01-run-20261122/kit. Max 10 submissions/day, 20 total; most recent before deadline is final; repo must be created after opening; agent transcripts required.

TASK: main.ts (Node 22, JS/TS only, no WASM/native/prebuilt binary) at a public GitHub repo root, whole repo <= 8,192 bytes. Runs 40 instances in one run (<= 60 s total, deterministic twice): each instance is program.bin + input.bin for make.fun's own tiny stack ISA; entry writes /output/<id>/stdout.bin + /output/<id>/exit.txt. ISA: 32-bit wrapping integers, 256-value stack, 64-deep call stack, 256 words of memory, input/output, 10 traps with distinct exit codes 2-11, 1,000,000-step limit, 65,536-byte output limit. Set = 26 ordinary programs + 14 edge cases, one hard ISA rule each. Final set drawn from drand round 34258812; practice set (round 34154306) is in the kit.

item.arguments:
{"message":"Build a STRONGER Sokoban v2 for Nicolas (@toyora) — a slim solver that can actually beat the perfect v1 on size WITHOUT losing optimality. You are the coordinator: fan out to your own subagents for research/build/verify as needed, but YOU own the submit decision and the run record. READ THIS WHOLE BRIEF — the guardrail at the end is absolute.

COMPETITION: sokoban-solver-01-run-20261121, FREE, $100 (10 x $10), deadline Mon 23 Nov 2026 10:00 WIB. V1 is already submitted and graded PERFECT 1,000,000 (submission 01a1fd74-5902-7099-9e5b-79bb79f049b0), but ranks ~942 because ties rank by size_bytes (v1 = 21,180 B; rank 1 = 754 B, rank 10 = 2,735 B). Quota: 1/6 used, 5 left. Force_Last: a new submission REPLACES v1 even if it scores lower — so a sub-perfect v2 would DESTROY the perfect standing entry.

WHAT ALREADY FAILED (do NOT repeat):
- User-pasted pure push-BFS (1,527 B, packed 1,098 B): perfect on practice, TIMEOUT 60s on freshB and freshC (dies on 16-17-push rooms — pure BFS explodes without a heuristic).
- User-pasted push-A* with distance-sum heuristic (1,826 B, packed 1,310 B): perfect on practice + freshA + freshB, TIMEOUT on freshC i005 (P*=61, rooms [15,16,16,14]; i005 alone ran >300s — one room shape explodes the distance-sum H).
- Lesson: the scored set is one random drand draw — a ~1-in-3 timeout chance would score 0 and replace the perfect v1. A v2 needs a STRONGER per-room search AND the same validation before submit.

YOUR DESIGN DIRECTION: per-room push search WITH dead-square + freeze pruning like v1 (v1: per-room push-A*, Hungarian-assignment heuristic, dead-square + freeze pruning, transposition table; worst room 8,431 expansions vs 200,000 cap; worst fresh set ~1.1s vs 60s), but golfed for size — target total <= ~2,600 B (aim ~2,400). The generator structure is PROVEN: rooms are independent (a box pushed through a door into the hallway can never return, so P* = sum of room optima); rooms can be found by cutting 1-wide door/hallway cells OR by arithmetic slot rectangles (slot s = cols [7s, 7s+7], above rows 0-8 / below rows 8-H-1).
